span.label: free recall —contrasted-with→ recognition memory
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER THE EVENT IS OBSERVABLE TO THE EXPERIMENTER. 'Whereas THE NEURONAL BASIS OF RECOGNITION MEMORY CAN BE PROBED EXPERIMENTALLY in human and nonhuman primates, Quotation withheld.' The two are not distinguished by any property of memory - they are distinguished by WHETHER THE EXPERIMENTER CAN SEE THE EVENT HAPPEN, so the division is one of experimental access and it explains why one literature is larger than the other. Q-475. · strength of the relation: 0.95

span.label: RETRACTED (NO RENAMING, AND THE SECOND ENDPOINT IS NOT IN THE SPAN) · replay —renamed-across-fields→ reactivation
span.note: RETRACTED: NO RENAMING, AND THE SECOND ENDPOINT IS NOT IN THE SPAN. The edge is `replay --renamed-across-fields--> reactivation`. The span reads: 'Quotation withheld' It names `replay` and links it to FREE RECALL - not to `reactivation`, which does not appear at all. A renaming names BOTH names; this names one and relates it to a third thing. Found by reading the whole `renamed-across-fields` untested population (Q-382), 21 of 21, where it is one of only three genuinely weak edges against ~18 that were sound. — strength of the relation: 0.65 — the record marks this weak
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (SAME FAULT, SAME PAPER, DIFFERENT ENDPOINT) · reinstated —renamed-across-fields→ reactivation
span.note: RETRACTED: SAME FAULT, SAME PAPER, DIFFERENT ENDPOINT. The edge is `reinstated --renamed-across-fields--> reactivation`. The span - 'brain activity present during the learning of information, as indirectly measured by the BOLD signal, IS REINSTATED during cued or free recall' - names `reinstated` and describes when it happens. `reactivation` is absent. Both this and [1] point at the same missing term, which suggests the tagger had a synonym set in mind that the paper never states in one place. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): that learning-period activity is reinstated at recall, measured by BOLD, with the fMRI caveat attached - a phenomenon, not a terminological equivalence, and it is already carried by other tags on this record. — strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — 2026-08-12: endpoint was 'BOLD signal', which is a measurement modality, not another NAME for the phenomenon. The renaming the quote reports is reinstated/reactivation. Caught by querying the corpus for the cross-vocabulary link this edge was recorded to provide, and finding it did not bridge.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A subset of human medial temporal lobe neurons fired selectively and in a sustained way throughout and after specific video episodes, for durations up to 12 seconds.

span.label: The same hippocampal and entorhinal neurons reactivated before the patient verbally reported freely recalling the corresponding episode.

span.label: The reactivation effect held at the population level in hippocampus and entorhinal cortex but was absent in medial frontal units, which were selective during viewing only.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In an individual recall trial, firing rose above baseline roughly 1.5 seconds before the verbal report and peaked shortly before speech onset, preceding rather than following the report.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Episode-specific reactivation was regionally graded: striking for hippocampal and entorhinal cells with sustained responses, weak in amygdala, and absent in parahippocampal gyrus.

span.label: Over half of all recorded units responded to at least one clip, with no difference in the proportion of responsive units across the sampled regions.

span.label: The results are unlikely to be an epilepsy artefact because responses were sparse and only a minority of units came from seizure foci, whose exclusion changed nothing.
